Eve_Customer: Hi — after the lingua-v3-adaptive rollout this morning we've seen p95 on /generate for long prompts (>6k chars) jump dramatically. Not seeing 5xx, just much slower responses.
Maya_Support: Can you paste a couple of request ids and approx time ranges? Any 429s/timeouts or just higher latency?
Eve_Customer: req_20260317_9a5c and req_20260317_b3f1, around 09:12-09:18 UTC. No 429/5xx, requests succeed but take ~1.1-1.3s p95 (was ~230ms). Payloads are emoji-heavy and lots of punctuation.
Maya_Support: Noted. Tagging infra/runtime/ml to triage. @Ravi_Infra @Jon_Runtime @Priya_ML
Ravi_Infra: digging into host metrics now — GPU and system mem fine. CPU on tokenizer worker threads spiked on those hosts. Looks CPU-bound.
Jon_Runtime: Can we compare token counts pre/post tokenizer change? If tokenization expanded that would explain extra decode work and KV cache pressure.
Eve_Customer: Pre-rollout token count for same prompt: ~960 tokens. Post-rollout: ~2,150 tokens (weird).
Priya_ML: That aligns with a subword explosion. lingua-v3-adaptive changed splitting heuristics to avoid incorrect merges around punctuation/ZWJ sequences; result is many small tokens for emoji clusters.
Maya_Support: Ok plan: 1) repro locally to confirm counts, 2) short-term mitigation for affected tenants, 3) long-term tokenizer fix.
Jon_Runtime: Short-term mitigation: route affected requests to the legacy tokenizer variant. We have a variant alias lingua-v3-legacy-tokenizer. You can override with header x-redwood-model-variant.
Maya_Support: Eve, can you test with this curl and confirm latency improves?
Maya_Support: ```
curl https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\" \
  -H \"x-redwood-model: lingua-v3\" \
  -H \"x-redwood-model-variant: lingua-v3-legacy-tokenizer\" \
  -d '{"input": "<your prompt>", "max_tokens": 512}'
```
Eve_Customer: Tried it — p95 returned to ~240ms, token count reported ~980. Looks fixed for these cases.
Ravi_Infra: Kicking off a canary rollback of the adaptive tokenizer config on the hosted pool (small % traffic).
deploy-bot: started canary rollback for lingua-v3-adaptive -> lingua-v3-legacy-tokenizer (canary_id: 20260317-c1).
deploy-bot: canary health check: 5m ok, latency delta restored for canary traffic.
Jon_Runtime: Additional urgents: i) set request-side clamp max_input_tokens for customers with very long emoji-dense inputs, ii) add per-request flag prefer_fast_tokenizer=true to select faster splitter, iii) enable prefix KV caching in routes where repeated prefixes are used heavily.
Priya_ML: Root cause details for tracking: adaptive padding preserved ZWJ/punctuation as separate subtokens leading to tokenization expansion on emoji clusters. We'll apply heuristics to re-merge common ZWJ emoji sequences and rare symbol clusters into single tokens.
Maya_Support: Action items and owners:
- Eve_Customer: confirm prod rollback mitigates across your tenants (assigned)
- Ravi_Infra: finish canary -> full rollback if canary stable (ETA 30m)
- Priya_ML: quick tokenizer patch to merge common emoji clusters, PR + tests (ETA 24h)
- Jon_Runtime: add telemetry metric tokenization_expansion_ratio = tokens_after / tokens_before and alert if >1.5 (ETA 48h)
Eve_Customer: Confirmed rollback fixed p95 in production. Thanks all :heart:
Maya_Support: Filing internal follow-up INF-2026-142 (tokenization regression: lingua-v3-adaptive). We'll keep you posted, closing this thread for now.
